visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md patterns, built from components/site/v3. No KB-era mockup — the pattern set is the target (same basis as every post-2026-08-27 page).
competitiveTarget: No Central Oregon brokerage has an investor destination at all — competitors bury multi-family in a search filter. This page wins by honesty: live per-type counts with the Market Truth trace, the rental math one tap away on every eligible listing, and NO cash-flow promises (the internal DSCR analysis shows Bend does not cash-flow on long-term rentals at financing rates; the page's stance is inventory + math, never hype).
note: Matt ruling 2026-09-01 (decisions.md): investor becomes a real job with /invest as the door and the listing-page investor lens as the depth layer. Every figure is a getPublicPlaceSegments region row — the same numbers the housing-market and search pages print (one source, §0). Stale internal analysis figures are never republished here. Capture is the income-property alert (multi-family pin — a narrowing filter). Detached/SFR is deliberately absent: that is the buyer story.

tasteReview.evaluator: separate claude-sonnet-5 evaluator agent, SITE-40 V3Quiet pass, session 019RdEm6 — the table instrument (first viewport at 1440x900 and 375x812, scripts/take-route-shots.mjs, scale 1, palette-quantized) captured by the coordinator against next dev (localhost:3198) on the lane branch with the lane's patch applied and main merged through 0ba0358d (SITE-42's source line) for /invest; three independent scorings of one capture run, the median; no page code read, no live page opened. The lane's Opus worktree agent had no Agent tool, so the coordinator ran the evaluators: round one on the lane's own captures (invest 38, compare 30, about 45, market-report 49, reviews 57, contact 49; about drew the scrolling-lists tell on seven glyph-marked doors, contact tied its table mark, and the market hub's source clauses read as internal labels), then a second pass after the class-level fixes — a face in the person door's mark slot, the reviews figure on the reviews door, plain-words source clauses (sourceName) with the trace behind the disclosure, the newest weekly snapshot on the Sales / weekly door — re-captured on the merged tree; then a third pass fixed the one honesty defect the second round named (the passage said the counts were below while the figure sat beside it) and re-captured; this receipt is that third round. The builder ran on Opus and did not grade its own page. The prior mark is the taste table of 2026-09-08 (median 25, scores 25·19·29), an instrument reading, not a route receipt (this file carried none).
tasteReview.beats: No win named — the shot shows one sourced live count and a methodology footnote, but no map, filter, chart, or segmentation; that is not yet more than what a saved Zillow or Redfin search already surfaces, so no demonstrable edge is visible in this viewport.
tasteReview.dullest: "How to underwrite here" — pure prose advice with no number, no source line, and no interactive element; it sits directly under the one part of the page that does have a figure, so it reads as the section a reader's eye slides past on the way down.
tasteReview.verdict: Real progress over the last mark: there is finally a figure with a source trace instead of two empty prose blocks, and the type, hairlines, and navy-on-cream discipline are genuinely on-brand. But it still reads like release notes with a stat pasted on top — two identically-shaped paragraphs under headers that explain the page to itself, one small toggle standing in for the interactivity a data page should deliver, and a right rail that runs out of things to say halfway down. Ship the number, then build the page around it — segment it, let it move — instead of writing about it.

defects.section: content row below hero ("What this page is" / "How to underwrite here")
defects.finding: The two body items repeat the identical heading-over-one-paragraph-over-hairline shape back to back, the same doc-style pattern the prior mark named on this route
defects.fix: Give the two items different visual treatments (e.g. one as a short numbered underwriting checklist, the other as plain copy) so no shape repeats twice in the same section

defects.finding: Headers 'What this page is' and 'How to underwrite here' read as internal documentation describing the page to itself, not a claim a visitor came for
defects.fix: Replace with a benefit-forward line the reader cares about, e.g. 'Every income listing on the MLS, priced for cash flow'

defects.finding: The one visible interactive affordance is a small 'how we calculate this' text toggle attached to methodology; the 762 count itself is not segmented (by multi-family / commercial / land / farm) or otherwise explorable, so the page's single data element rewards a tap with definitions, not with more data
defects.fix: Make the 762 figure break down by asset type on hover or tap instead of only exposing a methodology footnote

defects.section: right column below the source toggle
defects.finding: On desktop the right column runs out of content well before the left column does, leaving a tall empty gap beneath the toggle — a smaller echo of the empty-column defect named on the prior build
defects.fix: Either narrow the column to its content height or add one supporting figure (e.g. median cap rate) beneath the count
